record.what_it_does: CRM for Google Workspace users that manages leads, contacts, companies and opportunities.
record.auth_notes: There are two methods. (1) Per-user API key, token-based. Requests send the token plus the key owner's email and X-PW-Application: developer_api in headers. Copper says API keys are suitable for individual users, and third-party guides say only admins can generate them. (2) OAuth2, which Copper calls the preferred approach for partner integrations. You get a client_id and client_secret by contacting Copper at partners@copper.com. Only the developer/v1/all scope is supported.
record.access_notes: Copper is a paid CRM. The pricing page offers free trials ("Start free, no credit card required"). A third-party guide (JustCall) says Developer API access is limited to the Professional and Business plans, and Copper's pricing text does not show this per plan. Per-user API keys are self-serve on a qualifying plan. Multi-user OAuth needs manual registration by emailing partners@copper.com with the app name and purpose. There is no self-serve OAuth app creation.
record.api_breadth_notes: REST/JSON at https://api.copper.com/developer_api/v1. Docs sections cover Account and Users, Leads, People, Companies, Opportunities, Projects, Tags, Tasks, Activities, Custom Fields, Field Layouts, Related Items, File Upload and Webhooks. Each resource has CRUD and search operations. I did not count operations, but the total is likely about 50. A third-party n8n template exposes 32 operations, and StackOne exposes 58 tools.
record.mcp_notes: I found no official Copper MCP server: nothing on developer.copper.com and no Copper announcement. Third-party servers exist: StackOne (58 tools), Apideck, Activepieces, Zapier, Composio, Boomi, Scalekit, and community projects such as Cotlet's Copper CRM MCP server and one on Glama.
record.blocker_notes: Per-user API keys work for a prototype, but they need a paid or trial Copper account, reportedly on the Professional plan or higher. A proper multi-user OAuth app needs Copper to register it manually through partners@copper.com, and there is only one all-access scope. There is no dedicated sandbox, so testing uses trial accounts.

Also check whether Copper still responds to new OAuth partner registrations sent to partners@copper.com.
